pr_title: fix(trace-viewer): Rewrite file URIs in snapshots, like blob URIs.
pr_body:
This allows snapshots of file:/// pages with external stylesheets, images, etc to be rendered correctly in the trace viewer. (Otherwise, it tries to request the file:/// URIs directly and the requests get blocked by the browser.)

Fixes #31112.

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Trace viewer cannot load file:/// resources in snapshots
issue_context.body:
### Version

1.44.1

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/cartr/playwright-file-uri-trace-repro
2. `npm install; npm run test`
3. `npx playwright show-report`, and click on the "View trace" button to show the trace in the trace viewer
   - Alternatively, open `test-results/local-file-file-with-CSS/trace.zip` on https://trace.playwright.dev

### Expected behavior

The word "hi" appears in giant, bold, italic, purple Comic Sans.

### Actual behavior

The word "hi" appears in boring default Times New Roman.

This error is printed to the browser console when the trace viewer opens:

> Not allowed to load local resource: file:///[...]/playwright-file-uri-trace-repro/styles.css

### Additional context

I'm running the trace viewer in Microsoft Edge 125.0.2535.79 on Windows 11.

### Environment

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 6.5 Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS 22.04.4 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)
    CPU: (4) x64 AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor
    Memory: 14.45 GB / 15.61 GB
    Container: Yes
  Binaries:
    Node: 20.13.1 - /opt/hostedtoolcache/node/20.13.1/x64/bin/node
    Yarn: 1.22.22 - /usr/local/bin/yarn
    npm: 10.5.2 - /opt/hostedtoolcache/node/20.13.1/x64/bin/npm
  Languages:
    Bash: 5.1.16 - /usr/bin/bash
  npmPackages:
    @playwright/test: ^1.44.1 => 1.44.1
```

review_comments:
The thing this PR fixes is specifically related to loading a subresource, like a stylesheet, from a file URI. I think a text assertion would have already worked regardless, since the DOM snapshot just contains the text directly (as opposed to containing a `<link>` to the stylesheet, which the trace viewer then needs to load).

On Firefox it doesn't look like the trace file contains the stylesheet data. I didn't look closely into why, but it seems like a problem with _recording_ the trace, not viewing it. With WebKit, the test passes locally for me but not in CI, and I didn't debug why.

For future reference:

- Firefox does not issue a response for `file://` requests.
- WebKit does not return headers for `file://` requests and reports it with `status() = 0`
